\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Fourier Theory of Threshold Functions}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Fourier
\section{Overview}
This chapter relates polynomial threshold representations to Fourier uniqueness, low-degree spectral weight, noise sensitivity, and sparsity. It also records the flat spectrum and threshold sparsity of inner product modulo two, together with uniform sparse polynomial approximations.
\section{Declarations}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.ptf_chow_theorem}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube,BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThreshold,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.innerProduct_eval,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.eq_zero_of_expect_eq_zero,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_sub,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign_of_nonneg,BooleanAnalysis.expect,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff_empty,BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct,BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne}

Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E_x[h(x)\chi_S(x)]$ using uniform expectation, for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$.
Suppose $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$ for a real multilinear polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{|S|\le k}a_S\chi_S(x)$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
If $\widehat g(S)=\widehat f(S)$ for every $S$ with $|S|\le k$, then $g=f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier tail and noise sensitivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove_le_three_mul_noiseSensitivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseSensitivity,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseStability,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.one_sub_two_mul_pow_le_third,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff,BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne,BooleanAnalysis.parseval_pm_one,BooleanAnalysis.stability_formula}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, and define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
If $y$ is obtained from $x$ by flipping each bit independently with probability $\delta$, write $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)=\Pr[f(x)\ne f(y)]$; then
\[
 \sum_{|S|>\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor}\widehat f(S)^2
 \le3\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f).
\]
\end{lemma}

There exists $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ of the form $g(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$, where $p$ is a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$, with $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, such that
\[
 \Pr_x[f(x)\ne g(x)]\le3\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Correlation bounds low-degree Fourier weight]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sq_expect_abs_le_mul_fourierWeightUpTo}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThresholdRepresentation,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.expect_abs_eval_eq_innerProduct,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.innerProduct_eval,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo,BooleanAnalysis.expect,BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $p(x)=\sum_Sa_S\chi_S(x)$ have real coefficients with $a_S=0$ whenever $|S|>k$.
Suppose $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, and put $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ using uniform expectation.
Then
\[
 \bigl(\mathbb E_x|p(x)|\bigr)^2
 \le\left(\sum_Sa_S^2\right)\left(\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

 \qquad\text{and}\qquad

\]
\end{theorem}
